note: Rewritten from the original description by Mjöberg (1920); the original is in English (placed in the genus Hamitermes when published). The text was taken from the OCR of an Internet Archive scan, line-end word breaks are kept as in the original, and a few faulty OCR figures have been corrected from the context.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head dark brown; antennae 15-segmented; anterior margin of the pronotum slightly concave in the middle, anterior corners rounded, narrowing to rounded basal corners, posterior margin rather deeply concave in the middle, densely hairy, the surface with several small round yellow spots, the yellow mark behind the anterior margin and the median white line present. Forewing (Fig. 40 b in the original) pale rusty grey, rather short, the two strong veins of the anterior margin parallel and meeting before the rounded wing apex; usually a curved vein extends beyond the membranous part near the apex and turns sharply towards the wing apex, enclosing an oval area; the radius sector (mediana) forks from the middle of the wing, and two further branches usually fork near the apex; the cubitus with about 8—9 oblique, unbranched veins. Measurements: body length with wings 13 mm; body length without wings 7 mm; head length 1.4 mm; head width 1.12 mm; pronotum length 0.63 mm, width 0.93 mm; forewing length 10.2 mm, width 2.6 mm; hind wing length 9.9 mm, width 2.8 mm; abdomen width 2 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow, the mandibular apices and the middle tooth darker. Head distinctly longer than wide, posterior margin and sides rounded, apex convex, sloping downwards anteriorly; eyes represented by dark round spots on either side behind the antennal bases; clypeus small, anterior margin slightly concave, bilobed; labrum longer than wide, sides rounded, tapering towards the rounded apex, hairy; mandibles rather broad and curved, with an obtuse middle tooth near the middle; antennae 15-segmented, slender, pale yellow. Measurements: body length with mandibles 4.5 mm; head length with mandibles 1.81 mm; head length without mandibles 1.43 mm; head width 1.04 mm; pronotum length 0.38 mm, width 0.63 mm; abdomen width 1.33 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body white, head pale reddish yellow. Posterior margin and sides of the head rounded; lower margin of the base of the clypeus rounded, anterior margin truncate, apex strongly rounded; labrum broad and rounded; eyes as in the soldier, small dark round spots behind the antennal bases; mandibles as in the soldier but smaller, the dentition very similar; antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 nearly equal in length to segment 2, segments 4 and 5 round, about as long as wide, then gradually lengthening, segments 12—14 twice as long as wide. Measurements: body length 5 mm; head length 1.43 mm; head width 1.2 mm; pronotum length 0.34 mm, width 0.86 mm; abdomen width 1.51 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Small nests of variable shape and colour are built near tree roots, or dark round gallery balls up to the size of a walnut are built under dead wood; alates appear in November (month 11); specimens were collected at Colosseum, southern Queensland. It is distinguished from the other Australian species of the genus by the exceptionally large frontal gland (fontanelle), the very irregular wing venation, and the soldier head, which is reddish yellow and convex, with long mandibles bearing a distinct obtuse tooth; it is the only Australian species known to inhabit rainforest/dense forest.
